- Affected part: **stem** at the soil line
- White cottony/mycelial coating visible on the stem exterior near the soil line
- Plant is dead with wilted/dried leaves
- Roots visible at top, sandy soil around base

This strongly suggests **Southern Blight** (white mycelium at stem base, girdling at soil line). Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms Southern Blight pattern - a stem split longitudinally showing bleached/whitened interior tissue with dark necrotic border, matching the girdling infection pattern.

- White cottony mycelium on the stem exterior at soil line (hallmark of *Sclerotium rolfsii*)
- Stem girdling at the soil line causing plant collapse
- Dead/wilted plant tissue surrounding
- The stem split open showing bleached interior pith - consistent with the reference
